pages.text: "I eat it in one bite!" Gaga, who knew best, put a whole apple piece into their mouth. Stretching their neck, Gaga swallowed. Teacher Bau was adding more apple to the plate.
"See? I do not even chew." Before Lala, Gaga swallowed another whole piece. "I will finish fastest and go outside first!" Only two pieces remained.
But hic, hic! The hurried swallowing brought hiccups that would not stop. Timid Lala quickly pushed over a water cup. Gaga gulped water and finally caught their breath.
Outside, a little tummyache began. Gaga leaned against the wall and rubbed their belly. "Oh... first outside, but I cannot play."
Teacher Bau brought one apple piece and sat beside Gaga. Cutting it smaller and smaller, Teacher Bau laid out ten pieces. "Your mouth must make pieces small like this too. Ten chews for every bite!"
"Ten times?" Gaga looked between the big piece and the ten little ones. Teacher Bau counted ten claps. Clap, clap, clap... Gaga practiced moving their mouth.
At snack time the next day, Gaga took only a little bite. Chew, chew—one, two, three... ten, then swallow! "Oh? Sweet." Chewing spread sweetness through their mouth.
Teacher Bau sat nearby. "The mouth works first, so the tummy can be comfortable." Gaga nodded and chewed carefully again.
Now Gaga did not rush before an apple plate. "One, a little bite! Two, ten careful chews! Three, finish chewing, then swallow!" Gaga chewed to the last bite and stood up last.
Teacher Bau put an arm around Gaga's shoulders and went outside. Careful chewing meant no tummyache and better flavor. "Ten chews for every bite!" Gaga held Lala's hand and ran toward the swing.
